messages.subject: Conditionally enable controls
parts:
I am trying to conditionally enable (not hide)  an action button (or a selectInput), following the conditionalPanel example

conditionalEnabled <- function(condition, ...) {
  span('enable-if'=condition, ...)
}

    conditionalPanel(
      condition="input.PatientID == 'B'",
      actionButton("save","Save")
    ),
    conditionalEnabled(
      condition="input.PatientID == 'B'",
      actionButton("blub","Blub")
    )

I noted that I have to write the additional logic to attach the function like

dataDisplayIfFunc=function()

quite deeply nested in shiny.js. Is there an easier way to conditionally enable a control without hiding it?

Dieter

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Conditionally enable controls
parts: Hmmm, I'd have to think about this some more. This is a little different than data-display-if because displaying/hiding is easily accomplished using the same logic for any HTML element, whereas enable/disable would need custom logic depending on the type of control--we'd probably need to extend InputBinding with setEnabled(el, enabled) in order to support this properly.
